title: SDK Adapter Orchestration and Telemetry Playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Overview

This playbook documents recommended patterns and concrete examples for building SDK adapters and local runtime orchestration integrations that are resilient, observable, and easy for application engineers to adopt. It targets SDK maintainers, platform integrators, and runtime engineers who ship adapter code (sidecars, middlewares, language bindings) that interact with Redwood’s inference endpoints and local/private runtimes.

Goals

- Standardize adapter responsibilities: networking, authentication, retry/fallback, request shaping (batching/caching), and telemetry mapping.
- Provide sample artifacts (config templates, CLI snippets, telemetry mappings, and troubleshooting steps).
- Minimize on-ramp friction for app teams by enabling a one-command local orchestration dev loop that mirrors production routing/telemetry.

When to use this playbook

1. You are adding a new language binding or adapter (e.g., Rust client, JVM sidecar).
2. You need an adapter that performs local batching or request coalescing before sending to Redwood runtime.
3. You need consistent telemetry and error semantics across hosted and private deployments.

Design principles (short)

- Single responsibility: adapters should focus on protocol translation and best-effort performance optimizations; avoid business logic.
- Observable by default: every request must produce a trace, a latency metric, and a status tag.
- Resilient fallbacks: adapters should implement exponential backoff, per-route circuit breakers, and deterministic fallback rules (e.g., use cheaper model variant).
- Config-driven: behavior (batch windows, timeouts, model fallback lists) is controlled by a YAML config that can be overridden at runtime.

Adapter responsibilities (checklist)

- Authentication: acquire and rotate API token from process environment or KMS-backed local secret cache.
- Connection management: HTTP/2 persistent connections, TLS validation, idle connection pruning.
- Request shaping: batching, KV cache usage for repeated prefixes, request prioritization.
- Retries & circuit breakers: idempotency-safe retries for non-streaming requests; strict rules for streaming.
- Telemetry: emit trace/span per external call, metric for request_count, request_latency_ms (p50/p90/p99), model_variant tag, and error_reason.
- Local emulation: provide a dev mode to route to local mock runtime with deterministic outputs for unit tests.

Quickstart: local dev orchestration (one-liner)

1. Install the adapter CLI binary (example for macOS/linux):

   curl -sSfL https://internal-artifacts.redwood.ai/adhoc/sdk-adapter-cli/v0.3.1/install.sh | bash

2. Start the adapter in dev mode with sample config:

   adapter-cli start --env dev --config examples/dev-orchestration.yaml

3. Run the local coordinator to emulate Redwood routing and telemetry export:

   coordinator --load-config examples/coordinator-defaults.yaml --telemetry-console

The adapter automatically binds to localhost:4201 and exposes the same HTTP contract as the hosted SDK, so app teams can point their local service to http://localhost:4201 and get production-like behavior.

Example config (dev-orchestration.yaml)

---
adapter_name: example-java-adapter
listen: 0.0.0.0:4201
upstream: https://inference-api.redwood.ai/v1
auth: { type: env, token_var: REDWOOD_API_KEY }
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 16
  max_latency_ms: 15
fallbacks:
  - model_variant: small-quantized-v1
    condition: queue_depth > 100
circuit_breakers:
  - route: /v1/generate
    failure_threshold: 0.1
    window_seconds: 60
metrics_prefix: sdk.adapter.example
---

Telemetry mapping and examples

The adapter must emit the following signals to align with platform dashboards:

- trace/span: operation.name = "adapter.request"
  - tags: adapter.name, adapter.version, model.variant, route
- metric: sdk.adapter.request.count (tags: route, model.variant, status)
- metric: sdk.adapter.request.latency_ms (histogram)
- log line: structured JSON including request_id, user_id (if present), adapter.name, latency_ms, status_code, upstream_model

Example Prometheus metric names and labels (recommended):

- sdk_adapter_requests_total{adapter="java",route="/v1/generate",model="redwood-large-v2",status="ok"}
- sdk_adapter_request_latency_ms_bucket{le="50",adapter="java"} 42

OpenTelemetry sample (pseudo)

- Start a span around upstream call:

  span = tracer.start_span("adapter.upstream_call", attributes={"adapter.name": "example-java-adapter", "adapter.version": "0.3.1"})
  span.set_attribute("upstream.url", upstream)
  // inject context into request headers

- On error, record exception and set span.status = ERROR, attribute error.reason and error.code

API examples: shaping and retry behavior

1) Non-streaming generation (idempotent-ish):

   - On 5xx upstream error: retry up to 2 times with exponential backoff (100ms, 300ms), then return consolidated error to caller with error_code = upstream.temporary_failure.
   - On 429: if Retry-After header present, respect it; otherwise use backoff and consider enqueuing the request for batch retry if batching enabled.

2) Streaming generation:

   - Never retry a partially-delivered stream. If the connection fails before any tokens are delivered, adapter may retry if request is marked restartable.
   - Implement an at-most-once fallback: if upstream not available, return a short cached response or a structured error with suggestions for the client (see sample error shape below).

Sample error payload (JSON)

{ "error": { "code": "adapter.upstream_unavailable", "message": "Upstream model unreachable; request has been routed to fallback variant", "fallback_model": "small-quantized-v1", "request_id": "<uuid>" } }

Template: adapter healthcheck endpoint (HTTP)

- GET /healthz returns 200 when: TLS config loaded, able to open 1 connection to upstream within 200ms, config checksum matches runtime config.
- GET /live returns 200 when process is running.

Operational runbook (triage checklist)

1. Symptom: high p99 latency reported on sdk_adapter_request_latency_ms.
   - Step 1: check adapter logs for GC/latency spikes; correlate with host CPU and network egress.
   - Step 2: inspect batching metrics: current_batch_size_avg; if undersized, consider increasing max_batch_size or window.
   - Step 3: confirm upstream model variant is healthy (check platform model dashboard). If underlying model is slower, route to a faster variant via config.

2. Symptom: increased 5xx error rate from adapter upstream.
   - Step 1: identify error_reason tag on metrics. If TLS handshake fails, validate certs and SNI.
   - Step 2: verify API token validity (rotate token if near expiry).
   - Step 3: enable debug traces for a short window and capture a failed request trace.

3. Symptom: telemetry missing from dashboard after deploy.
   - Step 1: confirm the adapter exports OpenTelemetry; check aggregator connection (OTLP endpoint).
   - Step 2: check metrics prefix and label schema; adapters that miss required labels will be dropped by extractor jobs.

Release checklist for adapter maintainers

- Bump adapter semantic version and update changelog.
- Validate conformance to telemetry schema using the provided validator script:

  ./tools/telemetry-validator --schema adapters-v1 --endpoint http://localhost:4317

- Run integration smoke tests against staging coordinator (includes batch/stream variants):

  ./tools/adapter-smoke --staging --timeout 120s

- Create PR with config changes and include a short migration note for customers if defaults change.

Safety & compatibility notes

- Backwards compatibility: new adapter releases must preserve the public HTTP contract for 3 major versions or provide an opt-in compatibility flag.
- Secrets: do not log raw API keys or customer PII. Use redaction helpers in the standard logging library.

Appendix: helpful commands and scripts

- Generate a local adapter bundle for testing:

  ./build.sh && adapter-cli bundle --out /tmp/bundle.tar.gz --version v0.3.1

- Validate a YAML config against schema:

  yamllint examples/dev-orchestration.yaml && ./tools/config-validate --schema adapter-config-v2 examples/dev-orchestration.yaml

- Capture a full trace for a failing request (one-liner):

  TRACE=adapter* OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317 adapter-cli start --config examples/debug-config.yaml --trace-on-failure > /tmp/trace.json
